messages:
amanda: quick sync — following up on RFC for actor federation. ran into some edgecases when mixing org-scoped tokens with project-level RBAC. thoughts?
raj: short version: proxies see org tokens, can't easily enforce project-scoped grants. leads to either duplication of policy or overprivilege.
lina: is this mostly a telemetry/attestation gap or a token model gap?
amanda: both. example: background job uses org token to call router -> service-a. service-a needs to know original project intent to decide feature flags. right now we either pass extra headers (risky) or mint short-lived project tokens.
mike: minting short-lived tokens for every hop is expensive. latency and complexity spike (we tried that in small pilot).
raj: we could add an attestation flow: operator proxy attaches a signed claim that contains project_id + nonce. services verify signature against proxy key. no minting required.
lina: attestation sounds promising but raises audit + key-rotation complexity. who holds the proxy signing keys?
amanda: Dedicated proxies hold a key per region (KMS-backed). rotation is managed by infra, but we need a compatibility story for Private deployments.
mike: second pain: SDKs and runtimes expect bearer tokens for authn, not a separate attestation header. middlewares would need to change.
raj: suggestion: introduce a canonical header `X-Actor-Claim` with compact JWS (no nested JSON) — services validate via JWKS endpoint. keeps SDKs unchanged: bearer still used for authn, header used for authz.
lina: +1 but need to ensure we don't leak sensitive claims to downstream 3rd-party integrations. sanitize at ingress.
amanda: agreed. also thinking about fallback policy: if header absent, fall back to token-scoped checks. That preserves backward compatibility.
mike: can we add a lightweight CLI to simulate validation? e.g. `redwood-auth validate-claim --claim 'eyJ...' --service svc-a` — useful for debugging.
raj: good idea. Also add a feature flag to gate attestation checks while rolling out.
lina: question on RBAC mapping: do we map project roles into service-specific roles (role translation) or require services to interpret project roles directly?
amanda: prefer translation in the control plane (central mapping) so services remain simple. downside: control plane becomes the source of truth and a critical path for policy changes.
mike: tradeoff: central mapping simplifies services but makes rollouts harder and increases blast radius on mistakes. decentralized model keeps autonomy but inconsistent RBAC.
raj: practical compromise: central mapping + per-service overrides stored alongside service config. can be cached and pushed to services with TTL.
lina: cache invalidation story needed. default TTL 60s? and an emergency flush endpoint.
amanda: lifecycle thought: when migrating existing long-lived API keys, we can gradually attach `X-Actor-Claim` for new requests and enable server-side translate-to-claims for old keys for 30 days.
mike: logging: ensure both token id and claim are logged for correlation. add a `redwood/sec` structured field for analytics.
amanda: next steps: draft a short ops playbook (rotation, emergency revoke, attest header validation snippet) and a small RFC addendum with example code. @raj can you take the ops playbook?
raj: yes — will post a PR by EOD tomorrow.
lina: I'll prototype the middleware for node/python.
mike: I'll wire up the CLI validator and the logging hooks.
amanda: thanks. sec-bot: create ticket? :thumbsup:
sec-bot: created TICKET-3145 "actor-federation attestation rollout" and assigned to raj,lina,mike (link: https://tracker/internal/TICKET-3145)
amanda: perfect. keeping this thread as the check-in. :wave:
